tasks.short: Take attendance, keep enrolments and payments, write progress notes, check records are complete and send term figures to the administrator.

steps.what: Students enrol by e-mail and pay by bank transfer
Teacher takes attendance on a paper list each class
Teacher copies enrolments, payments and contact details from e-mails into a spreadsheet
Teacher writes progress notes per student in a document
Teacher checks the student records are accurate and complete before the term report
Teacher compiles attendance and enrolment figures for the administrator: by hand today; after the change the register drafts them and the teacher adds students who enrolled by e-mail
Teacher checks the term figures before they go: students, attendance and payments per class match the register and the known drop-outs
Teacher sends the checked term figures to the course administrator

tasks.design: Students enrol and pay in a booking tool for classes ({OTHER}), which creates their record; the teacher takes attendance on the phone in the same tool instead of on paper and writes progress notes, as today, in a notes field visible only to teachers. A missing-items list (payment, consent, contact) comes from the register. The register drafts the term figures; the teacher adds e-mail enrolments, checks the figures and sends them to the administrator once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Enrolments came by e-mail and lived in a spreadsheet next to paper attendance lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Class booking tools handle schedules, online booking and payment, memberships, attendance reports and messages.
tasks.still_hard: Progress notes still take thought; access must be limited to the people who need it.
tasks.human_edge: Remembering that a student missed classes because of illness and following up kindly.
tasks.altitude: Records keep themselves; the teacher writes only what needs judgement.

reach.task: Report enrolment and attendance per term
reach.learn: Whether register reports end chasing teachers for figures.

evidence.claim: A Dutch class booking tool offers schedules, online booking and payment, memberships, attendance reports and messaging.
Student records hold personal data; keep only what the course needs and limit access by role.

assumptions: Boundary: from enrolment to term figures; course pricing is outside.
Input contract: course schedule and prices set by the course administrator in the booking tool; enrolment data entered by students; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheet.
Administrator time is outside the teacher's savings.

Coverage: about 85% of students enrol and pay in the booking tool; the teacher still copies the rest from e-mails, so s2 keeps 20. Taking attendance and writing progress notes are first records and keep their full time (s1, s3). s4 keeps 50: the missing-items list replaces the search for gaps, but checking that records are right stays.
Students' enrolment time is priced as customer time, not as the teacher's savings.
unknowns: Whether the centre already uses a booking tool.
research_questions: Do online enrolments change who signs up?

already_counted.description: Teacher fixes items on the missing-items list.

incremental.description: Teacher answers students' questions about online enrolment and failed payments.
Course administrator sets up courses in the booking tool.
Students enrol, enter contact details and pay online themselves (work moved from the teacher's copying).

approvals.approved_version: The term figures per class (students enrolled, attendance and payments) exactly as checked by the teacher in s5b, sent once from the register to the course administrator for this term; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of students enrol online, so the teacher still copies about half the e-mails (s2 55) and adds more students to the figures by hand (s5 30) (32.9); high: about 85% enrol online as assumed (47.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch students practise, review what they hand in, note progress, tell them what to work on and check who falls behind the course objectives.

steps.what: Teacher watches students practise and gives suggestions for improvement in class
Teacher reviews practice pieces students hand in
Teacher writes each student's progress from memory after class
Teacher tells each student what to work on next
Teacher checks which students do not yet satisfy the course standards before term end

tasks.design: Right after class the teacher records a level per course objective for each student in the register of the class booking tool ({OTHER}) and adds a note if needed; this first record keeps its time. A term view lists who is behind on which objective; watching, reviewing and talking to students stay as they are, and no AI judges students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress lived in the teacher's memory and loose notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Class booking tools keep a register with attendance reports per student.
tasks.still_hard: Levels per objective are the teacher's judgement and take discipline to record.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a student is close to getting and giving the one tip that unlocks it.

reach.task: Check whether courses meet their objectives
reach.learn: Whether objective levels show which courses need changes.

evidence.claim: A Dutch class booking tool keeps attendance reports and messaging per student.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in education institutions is high-risk; this design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: from class practice to the term check; final grading is outside.
Input contract: course objectives set by the teacher in the register; fallback is notes.
Teaching, feedback and writing each student's progress keep their full time. s5 keeps 40: the term view replaces paging through notes, but judging who is behind stays with the teacher.
Levels are for the teacher and student only.
unknowns: Whether the booking tool supports objective levels.
research_questions: Do students who see their levels per objective practise more?

incremental.description: Teacher sets course objectives in the register once per course.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: levels are entered unevenly, so the teacher still pages through notes for most students (s5 70) (1.0); high: the term view is complete (2.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write test items, run oral and performance tests, mark closed items, judge open work and performances, record grades and issue certificates.

steps.what: Teacher prepares written test questions and tasks for each level

loop.input: The teacher's lesson notes for the level and the number and type of items wanted.
loop.output: A draft test with closed items, an answer key and two open tasks, each item tagged with the lesson it tests.
loop.check: Code checks that each closed item has exactly one keyed answer and a lesson tag that exists in the notes. The teacher reads every item against the lesson it is tagged to: does it test what was taught, is the key right, is the wording clear. Unclear items are rewritten by hand.
loop.stop: Approved, or after two redrafts the teacher writes the test.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fresh items each term from changing lesson notes cannot come from a fixed bank without students passing answers on.

steps.what: Teacher administers oral and performance tests in class
Students answer the closed items on the test form instead of on paper
Teacher marks closed written items: by hand today; after the change the form marks them against the key and the teacher checks flagged answers
Teacher judges open answers and performances against the criteria
Teacher records grades and fills certificates: by hand today; after the change the teacher enters each grade in the register and certificates fill from it
Teacher checks each student's grade and certificate before issue: name, course, level and grade match the teacher's own judgements
Teacher issues the checked grades and certificates to students

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts a written test with an answer key from the teacher's own lesson notes, and the teacher checks every item; students take the closed part on a form that marks it against the key. The teacher judges open work and performances and sets every grade, and certificates fill from the grades the teacher enters in the register. The teacher checks each grade and certificate and issues them once; no AI grades.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests were written from scratch and marked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors' AI tools rewrite and summarise text and pull word lists, and online forms mark closed items.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted items can be off-level or ambiguous; performances can only be judged by the teacher.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in a student's playing or speaking how far they have come.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks drafted items and keeps every grade.

reach.learn: Whether drafted items stay at the right level.

evidence.claim: A Dutch lesson editor's AI rewrites text at another difficulty, summarises and pulls word lists with definitions.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in education institutions is high-risk; here AI only drafts items and never grades.

assumptions: Boundary: from writing the test to issuing certificates; recognised external exams are outside.
Input contract: lesson notes written by the teacher; certificate template set by the course administrator; fallback is writing tests by hand.
No student data goes into the drafting step.
Oral and performance tests do not change.

s1 keeps 60: the draft saves writing closed items from scratch, but the teacher still reads and fixes every item and writes open tasks. s3 keeps 20 for checking flagged answers. s5 keeps 40 because entering each grade is the teacher's record of the decision; only copying onto certificates goes. Students answering on the form instead of paper (s2b) is not extra work for them.
unknowns: How many courses end with a written test.
research_questions: How often does the teacher change the key on drafted items?

already_counted.description: Teacher reads every drafted item and its key.

incremental.description: Teacher keeps lesson notes in a form the draft step can use.

approvals.approved_version: Each student's grade and certificate exactly as checked by the teacher in s5b, issued once to that student from the register; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: lesson notes are too thin to draft from, so the teacher writes tests as today (s1 100) (16.0); high: drafts are usable and the form marks closed items (24.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide what students should be able to do, write objectives per lesson, explain them in class and send them with the materials.

steps.what: Teacher decides what students should be able to do after each unit and project
Teacher writes clear objectives for all lessons in a new course plan each term
Teacher explains the objectives to students at the start of class
Teacher prepares each week's message with objectives and materials: written by hand today; after the change the booking tool fills it from the course plan
Teacher checks the week's message before it goes: objectives and materials match the lesson as now planned, files open, and it is addressed to this class
Teacher releases the checked message to the class through the booking tool

tasks.design: The course plan lives in one template in {DOCS} with objectives per lesson that the teacher reuses and adjusts each term instead of rewriting. Each lesson's message with objectives and materials is filled from the plan in the class booking tool's messages ({OTHER}); the teacher checks it and releases it the day before; deciding and explaining objectives stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were rewritten each term and objectives sent by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Class booking tools send messages to the students of each class.
tasks.still_hard: Good objectives come from knowing the students; reused plans can go stale.
tasks.human_edge: Making a student see why tonight's small step matters.

reach.learn: Whether shared plan templates make course descriptions consistent.

evidence.claim: A Dutch class booking tool includes messaging to the students of a class.
An AI tutor must tell users it is AI; this design has none.

assumptions: Boundary: from setting goals to students informed; teaching is outside.
Input contract: course plan template kept by the teacher; class lists from the booking tool; fallback is e-mail.

Deciding and explaining keep their full time. s2 keeps 60: the teacher reuses last term's objectives but reads and adjusts each one. s4 keeps 20 for fixing the filled message; checking and releasing it are their own steps.
Courses repeat at least once a year.
unknowns: How often courses repeat with the same content.
research_questions: Do students who get objectives in advance prepare more?

incremental.description: Teacher keeps material links in the course plan current each term.

approvals.approved_version: This week's message with its objectives and materials exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once through the class booking tool's messages to this course's class list; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the course runs only once, so objectives are written fresh (s2 100) (9.9); high: the course repeats and last term's plan is reused (17.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The self-enrichment teacher keeps teaching, judging and encouraging; records, figures and weekly messages run from the booking tool.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose admin fits in ten minutes after class and whose students always know what they are working towards.
